advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a total-order tiebreak (e.g. include a canonical payload/provenance hash) to the intra-group mutation sort in plan_pass, or document why (direction, action) is guaranteed unique within a target.
evidence: mutation.py identity is (direction, action, target); target is constant within a group, so the sort key has no total-order tiebreak for same direction+action within one target
advisory.finding: Within a single target group, plan_pass sorts mutations only by (m.direction.value, m.action.value); two mutations in the same target sharing that pair are ordered only by the stability of the input sequence, so plan-internal ordering (and thus TicketPlan equality/hash) is not guaranteed deterministic if such a collision ever occurs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion pinning the sorted order of REB-200's two mutations (e.g. `(inbound, update)` before `(outbound, update)` per the `(direction.value, action.value)` key).
evidence: test_plan_pass_groups_mutations_by_target asserts only `len(by_identity["REB-200"].mutations) == 2` and `{m.target ...} == {"REB-200"}` — no assertion on the ORDER of the two REB-200 mutations
_mutations() supplies REB-200's mutations unsorted: `(outbound, update)` before `(inbound, update)` — the named input that exercises the sort but whose sorted output is never verified
advisory.finding: The within-plan mutation ordering (sort by `(m.direction.value, m.action.value)`) added at ticket_planner.py:89-90 is never asserted. REB-200 receives two mutations supplied deliberately unsorted (outbound/update, then inbound/update), yet the tests only assert the count (`len == 2`) and target set for REB-200, so a regression that dropped or reversed the sort key would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_plan_pass_groups_mutations_by_target assert `[(m.direction.value, m.action.value) for m in by_identity["REB-200"].mutations] == [("inbound","update"),("outbound","update")]`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the emitted plan identities equal the SORTED sequence, e.g. `[p.identity for p in plans] == sorted({m.target for m in mutations})`.
evidence: test_plan_pass_is_deterministic asserts `plans_a == plans_b` and `[p.identity for p in plans_a] == [p.identity for p in plans_b]` — both sides are the SAME code path, so equal-but-unsorted output passes
test_plan_pass_groups_mutations_by_target checks `set(by_identity) == {...}` — set comparison discards order
No test asserts the emitted identities equal the sorted sequence `["REB-200","REB-300","local-9"]`
advisory.finding: The emitted plan ORDER (targets emitted via `sorted(grouped)` at ticket_planner.py:88) is never asserted as sorted; the determinism test is a convergence twin that compares two runs of the same code path and would stay green even if the planner did not sort targets at all.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert [p.identity for p in plans_a] == sorted({"local-9","REB-200","REB-300"})` (Python sort → `['REB-200','REB-300','local-9']`) in the deterministic/grouping test.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] In run_differs' plan_pass call, extract the mode via `getattr(ctx.target_mode, 'value', ...)` (matching reconcile.py) instead of `str(...)`, so a Mode enum yields 'live' not 'Mode.LIVE'.
evidence: mode.py:30: `class Mode(str, Enum):` — a custom (str, Enum) whose str() returns the member repr ('Mode.LIVE') on Python 3.11+, not the value
reconcile.py:112: `target_mode: Any = None` (real ctx carries a Mode enum member)
reconcile.py:292: established idiom `mode=target_mode.value if target_mode else "live"`; reconcile.py:794: `getattr(target_mode, "value", str(target_mode))`
pyproject.toml:16: `requires-python = ">=3.11"` — the version where str() on a (str,Enum) yields the member-qualified repr
blocking.finding: run_differs passes mode=str(getattr(ctx,'target_mode','') or '') to plan_pass, but ctx.target_mode is a Mode(str, Enum) member; on Python 3.11+ str(Mode.LIVE) returns 'Mode.LIVE', not the canonical 'live'. The observation's mode field and its content-hash fingerprint therefore capture the mangled enum repr instead of the mode value used everywhere else in the codebase.
blocking.suggested_fix: Use the codebase idiom: `mode=getattr(getattr(ctx, "target_mode", None), "value", "") or str(getattr(ctx, "target_mode", "") or "")` — or normalize target_mode to its .value before the call, matching reconcile.py:292/794.
